blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Most AI-generated video detectors analyze decoded pixels and overlook how videos are produced. We show that causal video autoencoders leave an architecture-specific rhythm in compressed bitstreams: their temporal stride concentrates unpredictable content at latent-chunk boundaries, so rate-distortion optimized encoders allocate bits periodically. Without decoding pixels, we observe four-frame pulses in CogVideoX and Wan2.2 and eight-frame pulses in LTX-Video, which are absent from content-matched camera footage. Passing camera footage through a generator's autoencoder alone induces the pulse, supporting its proposed origin. A training-free peak-ratio statistic separates generated from camera video (AUC 0.84-0.94) and persists across tested quantization settings and H.264/H.265 encoding. Frame-size traces also identify four commercial generators, with 89.2%, 84.1%, and 83.0% accuracy under H.264, H.265, and AV1, beating the pixel-based UnivFD baseline (72.7-73.6%). Our results directly link generative architecture to measurable coding demand.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Text-to-video and image-to-video generators now produce clips that are hard to tell from camera footage by eye [ 13 , 3 , 22 , 21 ] .
Much work detects AI-generated images, and increasingly video, from decoded pixels [ 24 , 15 , 23 ] .
Far less links detection to the generative process itself, perhaps because a delivered video is shaped not only by the generator but also by a video encoder, a system many vision researchers rarely look inside.
This paper follows a generated video through both.
blocks.zh:
文本到视频和图像到视频的生成器现在产生从镜头镜头中难以从眼睛分辨的片段[13,3,22,21].
许多工作都从解码像素中检测AI生成的图像,并越来越多地检测视频[24,15,23].
更少连接到基因过程本身的检测,也许是因为传送的视频不仅由生成器塑造,而且由视频编码器塑造,这个系统许多视觉研究者很少在内部查看.
本文通过这两段视频,

blocks.en:
Nearly all current generators are latent generators: a diffusion or flow model samples a compact latent video, and a video autoencoder decodes it to pixels [ 29 , 21 , 12 ] .
To compress time, these autoencoders are causal 3-D networks with a fixed temporal stride s s : the first frame is decoded alone, and every later latent frame is decoded into s s pixel frames.
Call the part of a frame that cannot be predicted from its past its surprise .
In camera footage, surprise arrives continuously, at roughly the same rate in every frame.
We propose that in a latent video it can enter only where a new latent frame enters, once every s s frames, since the frames in between are decoded from the same latent.
Generated video should then carry a surprise rhythm with period s s , locked in phase to the latent-chunk grid ( Fig. 2 ).
The stride is an established architectural fact; the rhythm is the mechanism we propose and test.

blocks.en:
The second half of the pipeline is a conventional video encoder.
Codecs such as H.264/AVC [ 25 ] , HEVC [ 20 ] and AV1 predict each frame from frames already coded and are rate–distortion (RD) optimized [ 19 ] : they spend bits only on what their temporal prediction cannot anticipate, that is, on surprise ( Fig. 3 ).
The bits an encoder spends on each frame, readable from the bitstream without decoding, should therefore trace the generator’s rhythm. Figure 1 shows that they do.
Re-encoded under identical settings, clips from CogVideoX [ 29 ] and Wan2.2 [ 21 ] (stride 4) pulse every fourth frame and clips from LTX-Video [ 12 ] (stride 8) every eighth, while content-matched camera clips do not pulse; a training-free peak ratio separates them at an AUC of 0.84–0.94.
blocks.zh:
管道的下半部是一个传统的视频编码器.
H.264/AVC[25],HEVC[20]和AV1等编解码器从已经编码的帧中预测出每个帧,并且被率-扭曲(RD)优化[19]: 他们只花点时间预测所无法预料的东西,即出乎意料(图3)。
编码器花费在每一帧上的比特,从比特流可以读取而不解码,因此应该追踪生成器的节奏. 图1显示它们确实如此。
在相同的设置下重新编码,剪辑来自CogVideoX [29]和Wan2.2 [21](第4步),每四帧脉冲和剪辑来自LTX-Video [12](第8步),而内容匹配的相机剪辑不脉冲;在0.84–0.94的AUC中,没有训练的峰值比将其分开.

blocks.en:
We tell the story in three steps.
First, the pattern originates in the latent representation: the pulse frequency moves with the stride, its phase follows the chunk grid for the stride-4 models, and passing camera clips through a generator’s autoencoder alone creates it ( Secs. 3 and 6 ).
Second, it survives video encoding: in both H.264 and H.265, and from quantization parameter (QP) 22 to 37 (AUC 0.92 to 0.80) ( Secs. 4 and 6 ).
Third, its persistence has limits we state plainly: delivery-style encodes with rate control and B-frames erase the per-frame pulse in 14 of 15 tested cases, although x265 still places its reference frames on the stride-4 grid.
blocks.zh:
我们分三步讲述这个故事.
首先,图案起源于潜在的表达方式:脉冲频率随步态而移动,其相位随步态-4模型的块网格而移动,光通过一个发电机的自动编码器而传递的相机片段就会产生它(第3和第6节)。
第二,它存活于视频编码:在H.264和H.265中,以及从量化参数(QP)22到37(AUC 0.92到0.80)(secs. 4和6).
第三,它的持久性有局限性,我们明确指出:在15个试验病例中,有14个病例的交付式编码具有速率控制,B帧擦除每帧脉冲,尽管x265仍然将其参考框架放在脚步-4网格上。

blocks.en:
The traces are simple to read ( Sec. 5 ).
We divide each frame’s size by the clip’s mean, giving frame-size ratios, and feed them to a logistic regression or to a small transformer with 26K parameters.
We evaluate on DeepAction [ 4 ] , 2,605 clips of human actions from camera footage and six generators, and on a self-collected Frontier dataset of four commercial generators (Grok, HeyGen, MiniMax, Wan) on 40 shared prompts, with 160, 159 and 155 clips re-encoded in H.264, H.265 and AV1.
On Frontier, where all generators share frame size and length, the logistic regression identifies the generator at 89.2%, 84.1% and 83.0% in H.264, H.265 and AV1, and the transformer at 80.6% and 78.4% in H.264 and H.265 (chance 25%); on the same clips and task, the pixel-based UnivFD detector [ 15 ] reaches 72.7%, 73.6% and 73.4%, so bitstream traces outperform it by 10–17 points.
The advantage is specific to this generator-identification task: for camera versus generated video on DeepAction with size and length controlled, UnivFD remains stronger (90.5% vs. 69.9–74.1% balanced accuracy on 16-frame crops, known generators), while gradient-boosted trees on bit statistics reach 88.8% on 192-frame clips.
On DeepAction we equalize frame size and clip length throughout, since its sources differ in file format, and a classifier that works need not use the rhythm, which we test with ablations and attributions ( Secs. 6 and 6 ).

blocks.en: Our contributions are two: • Linking temporal compression in video generation to a detectable trace. To our knowledge, we are the first to tie a video generator’s temporal stride to a measurable trace, as prior work did for spatial up-sampling and autoencoders in images [ 10 , 9 , 17 ] . • A decoding-free method that reads the rhythm directly from the encoded bitstream. CoDe takes frame and row sizes from the bitstream without reconstructing pixels and identifies four frontier commercial generators at 83.0–89.2%, against 72.7–73.6% for the pixel-based UnivFD

blocks.en: 2 Background and Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 背景和有关工作

blocks.en:
CNN-generated images carry traces that a classifier trained on one generator can detect in others [ 24 ] , and frequency analyses attribute many of them to up-sampling layers [ 10 , 9 ] .
Large pretrained features generalize better to unseen generators [ 15 ] , diffusion images leave weaker traces [ 8 ] , and the reconstruction error of a latent model’s autoencoder exposes images it generated [ 17 ] .
B-Free [ 11 ] removes content, format and resize biases one at a time; we adopt the same discipline for video ( Sec. 6 ).
For video, synthetic-image detectors fail on synthetic video, compression is not the main reason, and video generators leave traces a learned detector finds even after H.264 re-compression [ 23 ] .
Spatio-temporal detectors trained on GenVideo [ 7 ] and training-free detectors that model the likelihood of real video [ 2 ] extend this line.
All of these operate on decoded pixels; we instead analyze how a video encoder allocates its bits, read from the bitstream without reconstructing pixels.
blocks.zh:
有线电视新闻网生成的图像带有在一台发电机上受过训练的分类器能在其他发电机中检测到的痕迹[24],频率分析将其中很多图像归结为上采样层[10,9].
大型预先训练的特性更能概括为看不见的生成器[15],扩散图像留下较弱的痕迹[8],潜在模型的自动编码器的重建错误暴露了它生成的图像[17].
B-Free [11] 一次去掉一个内容、格式和大小的偏差;我们对视频采用同样的纪律(第6条)。
对于视频来说,合成图像探测器在合成视频上失效,压缩不是主要原因,视频生成器甚至在H.264重新压缩[23]之后仍然留下一个学习的探测器发现的痕迹.
接受过GenVideo[7]培训的spatio-时空探测器,以及模拟真实视频可能性的无训练探测器[2]扩展了这条线.
所有这些都运行在解码像素上;我们转而分析一个视频编码器如何分配它的比特,从比特流读取而不重建像素.

blocks.en:
CogVideoX [ 29 ] and Wan [ 21 ] use causal 3-D autoencoders with temporal stride s = 4 s{=}4 , in which the first frame is encoded alone and every later latent frame summarizes four pixel frames; LTX-Video [ 12 ] compresses time by s = 8 s{=}8 .
The stride is an architectural constant, shared by every clip a model produces, whatever its content or sampler.
Reconstruction by a latent model’s autoencoder already exposes generated images [ 17 ] ; we study the effect of the autoencoder’s temporal structure on the generated video, and use the resulting rhythm for classification.
blocks.zh:
CogVideoX [29] 和 Wan [21] 使用因果 3-D 自动编码器,其时步 S = 4 s{=}4 ,其中第一个帧单独编码,每个后期的潜伏帧概括四个像素帧; LTX-Video [12] 压缩时间为 s = 8 s{=}8 .
脚步是一个建筑常数,由模型制作的每一个片段共享,无论它的内容或采样器如何.
通过潜在模型的自动编码器进行重建已经暴露出生成的图像[17];我们研究了自动编码器的时间结构对生成的视频的影响,并利用由此产生的节奏进行分类。

blocks.en:
Hybrid codecs such as H.264/AVC [ 25 ] and HEVC [ 20 ] predict each block from the same frame (intra) or from reference frames (inter) and code the residual.
Frames form groups of pictures (GOPs) that begin with an intra-coded I-frame, followed by predicted P- and B-frames.
For each block the encoder minimizes J = D + λ ​ R J=D+\lambda R [ 19 ] , with λ \lambda set by the quantization parameter (QP).
The resulting allocation is an operational estimate of the content’s rate–distortion function [ 18 ] as seen through the encoder’s predictors, and when frames depend on each other the optimal allocation favors heavily referenced frames [ 16 ] .
Rate control (constant QP, constant rate factor (CRF), target bitrate), adaptive quantization and MB-tree then move bits in space and time, which is why the encoder and its settings are part of our measurement.
Holding these settings fixed (constant QP, one I-frame followed by P-frames, adaptive tools off) removes the encoder’s own patterns, so the bit allocation that remains can be studied as a property of the content ( Sec. 6 ).
blocks.zh:
H.264/AVC[25]和HEVC[20]等混合编码器从同一个框架(内部)或参考框架(间)预测每个区块,并编码剩余部分.
帧组成图片组(GOPs),从编码内部的I帧开始,然后是预测的P-和B帧.
每个块的编码器最小化 J = D + + + + + r = D + lambda R [19],由量化参数(QP)设置的\\lambda.
由此得出的分配是从编码器的预测器中可以看出的内容率-扭曲函数[18]的操作估计,当帧互相依赖时,最优的分配偏好是大量引用的帧[16].
速率控制(恒定QP,恒定速率因子(CRF),目标比特率),适应性量化和MB-tree然后在时空移动比特,这就是编码器及其设置是我们测量的一部分的原因.
持有这些设置固定(恒定QP,一个I-frame跟随P-frame,适应性工具关闭)可以去除编码器自己的模式,因此留下的位分配可以作为内容的属性来研究(sec. 6).

blocks.en:
Motion vectors and residuals support action recognition without full decoding [ 26 ] , and entropy-based compression statistics were recently shown to form a rich and highly efficient spatial–temporal representation for video understanding [ 1 ] .

These works recognize what a video shows.
Closest to us, codec motion-vector statistics have been used to rate the temporal realism of generated video [ 5 ] ; that study reports oscillations in per-frame averages but attributes them to interpolation and resamples clips to a common length, which would blur a native stride rhythm. The same group showed that frame-type counts identify which corpus a clip came from [ 6 ] , the confound our protocol is built to remove.
We ask what the encoder’s bit allocation reveals about how a video was made; to our knowledge, a stride-locked rhythm in encoder bits has not been reported before.
blocks.zh:
运动向量和残余支持动作识别而无需完全解码[26],最近显示,基于肽的压缩统计为视频理解提供了丰富而高效的空间-时态表现[1].

这些作品能识别视频显示的内容.
与我们最接近的是,已使用编码运动-载体统计数据来评价生成的视频的时间现实主义[5];该研究报告每帧平均值的振荡,但将它们归结为插值和复标片片段的共通长度,这会模糊原生速度节奏. 同一组人显示 帧式的计数 识别出从 [ 6] 的哪一个弹夹, 混淆我们的协议是用来删除的。
我们问编码器的比特分配揭示了录像是如何制作的; 据我们所知, 编码器比特中节奏的步调以前还没有报道过。

blocks.en:
A modern encoder such as HEVC [ 20 ] codes a video as a group of pictures (GOP).
An intra (I) frame is coded on its own, like a still image.
A predicted (P) frame is coded as a prediction from an earlier, already decoded frame (motion-compensated copying of blocks) plus a residual , the part the prediction got wrong.
A bidirectional (B) frame may also predict from a later frame.
The residual is quantized with a step size set by the quantization parameter (QP; larger means coarser) and entropy-coded.
The encoder is rate–distortion (RD) optimized: for each block it chooses the mode, motion and quantized residual that minimize J = D + λ ⁡ ( QP ) ​ R J=D+\lambda(\mathrm{QP})\,R , distortion plus λ \lambda times rate [ 19 ] .
At a fixed QP, what a P-frame costs is therefore what its predictor could not anticipate, i.e . its surprise ( Fig. 3 ).

Does generated video carry a bit rhythm at the autoencoder’s stride, and camera video not?
Both stride-4 generators peak at exactly f = 1 / 4 f{=}1/4 , with a harmonic at 1 / 2 1/2 , and the stride-8 generator at exactly 1 / 8 1/8 ; camera clips at their native rate show no peak ( Fig. 5 ).
The median peak ratio at the generator’s own stride is 27–29 for CogVideoX and Wan2.2 and 6.1 for LTX-Video, against 1.1–1.4 for their camera references ( Tab. 1 ). The AUC is 0.84–0.94 with x265 and 0.85–0.93 with x264 (CogVideoX, Wan2.2, LTX-Video: 0.85, 0.90, 0.93).
Generated video does not have a flatter bit spectrum than camera video; it concentrates the temporal variation of its bits at the stride frequency.
Doubling the stride moves the peak from 1 / 4 1/4 to 1 / 8 1/8 : LTX-Video has PR 8 = 6.1 \mathrm{PR}_{8}{=}6.1 but PR 4 = 2.4 \mathrm{PR}_{4}{=}2.4 , whereas the stride-4 generators have PR 8 \mathrm{PR}_{8} of 0.6–1.4.
The scenes are shared across generators, so only the stride explains the shift.
If the rhythm comes from latent chunks, removing the first k k frames must rotate the peak residue by k k .
For Wan2.2, 85–95% of encodes match the predicted residue across k ∈ { 1 , 2 , 3 } k\in\{1,2,3\} and time reversal; for CogVideoX, 58–75% (chance 25%).
LTX-Video is periodic at 1 / 8 1/8 , but only 23–58% of its encodes match (chance 12.5%), and its excess spreads over the first half of the chunk ( Fig. 1 b).
The phase prediction thus holds for stride 4 and fails for LTX-Video, whose decoder evidently does not place each chunk’s new content on its first frame.

We pass each camera clip through each generator’s autoencoder (official weights; encode, take the latent mode, decode) and encode the round-trip clip exactly like the original; shifts k ∈ { 0 , 1 , 2 } k\in\{0,1,2\} drop k k leading frames before the round trip.
The decision rule was registered before any round-trip data existed: median PR s > 3 \mathrm{PR}_{s}{>}3 , AUC ≥ 0.75 {\geq}\,0.75 against the originals, and a phase locked to one residue at every k k for at least 50% of clips.
All three autoencoders create the rhythm ( Tab. 2 ). CogVideoX’s raises the median peak ratio from 1.4 to 87.0 (AUC 0.99); Wan2.2’s and LTX-Video’s reach 12.9 and 10.4. The modal residue is t ≡ 1 ( mod s ) t\equiv 1\pmod{s} for all three at every shift, held by 75% of CogVideoX clips and 60–65% of Wan2.2 clips, but only 30–50% of LTX-Video clips, so LTX-Video is only partially supported. x264 agrees (AUC 0.81–0.995).
The autoencoder is therefore sufficient to produce the rhythm, without the sampler.

Can a classifier trained on coding demand tell generators apart?
We train the two detectors of Sec. 5 , a small Transformer on per-frame (or per-row) bits and gradient-boosted decision trees (GBDT), and two simple models on per-frame bits, a logistic regression (LR) and a two-layer perceptron (MLP, 32 hidden units), and compare them with UnivFD [ 15 ] on decoded pixels and a size probe , a logistic regression on frame width × {\times} height alone.

All four generators of the Frontier set share frame size and length, so format cannot help ( Tab. 5 ).
A logistic regression on per-frame bits normalized by the clip mean identifies the generator at 89.2%, 84.1% and 83.0% (H.264, H.265, AV1), at least as well as the Transformer and trees and 9.6–16.5 points above UnivFD on decoded frames (72.7–73.6%); the size probe is at chance (25.0–25.4%). AV1 files carry 84 hidden reference frames per clip and the encoder’s own reference pyramid; since LR still reaches 83.0% on AV1, the drop of the Transformer and trees there is a failure of those models, not a lack of signal.

DeepAction’s sources differ in frame size and clip length, and accuracy drops once these are equalized ( Tab. 6 ), so we compare detectors on crops of equal size and length.
Natively, binary CoDe ties UnivFD [ 15 ] (94.9% vs. 93.9% known, 87.0% vs. 86.4% on held-out generators), but so does the size probe on width × {\times} height alone (96.0% and 89.4%). On 16-frame crops, where the size probe falls to 50.0%, UnivFD keeps 90.5% and 85.9%, while CoDe reaches 69.9–74.1% and 67.3–70.0%, and motion-vector statistics [ 26 ] 71.4% and 68.8% ( Tab. 7 ).
With format controlled on DeepAction, pixels thus beat coding demand on 16-frame crops, unlike on the Frontier set ( Tab. 5 ); the advantage of coding demand here is cost: parsing takes 0.31–0.37 s per clip vs. 3.9 s for UnivFD’s decode (H.264 input needs a ≈ 45 {\approx}45 s re-encode).

Where in time does the trained classifier look?
For the WPP Transformer trained on the H.265 Frontier set (21 training, 5 test clips per class) we compute integrated gradients (IG) and attention rollout on its 32-band × {\times} 192-frame input, sum | IG | |\mathrm{IG}| over bands, and measure its share on the I-frames ( t ≡ 0 mod 16 t\equiv 0\bmod 16 ) and, among the other frames, on each residue mod 4.
IG concentrates on keyframes: 21–57% of its mass falls on the 6% of frames that are I-frames ( Tab. 8 ).
Among the other frames there is no 4-frame grid (residue-0 share 0.21–0.24, uniform 0.20), and the top residue is 0 in every class, including Wan (predicted: 1).
Attention rollout is temporally uniform.
On DeepAction, IG on CogVideoX’s chunk-start frames is 0.200 (uniform 0.267), though they carry 5.9% more bytes.
The attributions thus follow the encoder’s I-frame schedule, not the autoencoder’s grid, yet that intra-frame cost is not necessary: retrained on P-frames only, the detectors reach 76.6–87.5%, within 2 points of all frames. Retraining shows sufficiency, not use; a test-time ablation was not run.

Is the rhythm carried by individual blocks of the frame, and does the autoencoder’s spatial compression leave a grid?
Under registered rules we compute each block’s own PR s \mathrm{PR}_{s} for AV1 64 × 64 64{\times}64 superblocks (libaom real-time mode, fixed quantizer) and x265 rows of coding blocks.
The share of active superblocks with PR s > 3 \mathrm{PR}_{s}{>}3 is 0.62, 0.60 and 0.31 for generated CogVideoX, Wan2.2 and LTX-Video, 0.60, 0.29 and 0.32 for round trips, and 0.11–0.13 for camera (noise floor ≈ 0.12 {\approx}\,0.12 ); x265 rows reach 1.0, 1.0 and 0.50.
By the rule ( ≥ 0.50 {\geq}\,0.50 ) the rhythm lives inside blocks for CogVideoX and generated Wan2.2, not for the Wan2.2 round trip or LTX-Video (clear only per row or frame), and is strongest in textured blocks (Spearman 0.59–0.61 with texture, 0.10–0.30 with motion).
Decoded pixels show no stationary grid at the spatial factors 1 / 8 1/8 , 1 / 16 1/16 , 1 / 32 1/32 (medians ≤ 1.11 {\leq}\,1.11 ; rule: 3), only a few percent of excess power (AUC 0.70–0.97, also after round trips); post hoc, LTX-Video has a horizontal-only line at 1 / 8 1/8 (median PR 13.9 generated, 13.3 round trip, 1.0 camera).
The temporal compression thus makes the rhythm, block by block; the spatial compression leaves at most a faint grid.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: We reveal a previously unrecognized link between how AI videos are generated and how they are compressed. A latent video generator’s temporal autoencoder leaves an architectural fingerprint: a periodic rhythm in temporal surprise, determined by its latent stride and chunk boundaries. Conventional video encoders translate this hidden rhythm into measurable fluctuations in coding demand, exposing the generator’s internal structure directly in the compressed bitstream, without reconstructing a single pixel.
blocks.zh: 我们揭示了AI视频是如何生成和如何压缩之间的一个先前未识别的链接. 一个潜在的视频生成器的时间自动编码器留下了一个建筑指纹:一个时间惊喜的周期性节奏,由它的潜在步态和块状边界决定。 常规视频编码器将这种隐藏的节奏转化为可测量的编码需求的波动,直接在压缩位流中暴露出生成器的内部结构,而不重建单个像素.

blocks.en: We trace this fingerprint to its source. A video’s period follows the autoencoder stride, its phase aligns with latent chunk boundaries, and an autoencoder round trip alone induces the rhythm in camera footage. The trace persists across codecs and quantization settings, although delivery-style encoding can erase the per-frame pulse. Beyond this specific rhythm, lightweight classifiers exploit coding-demand statistics to identify four commercial video generators with 83–89% accuracy, significantly outperforming pixel-based approach.
blocks.zh: 我们追踪到指纹的来源 一段录像时间跟随自动编码器脚步, 追踪在编码器和定量设置之间持续存在,尽管交付式编码可以抹去每帧脉冲. 除了这种特定的节奏外,轻量级分类器还利用编码需求统计来识别4台精度为83-89%的商业视频生成器,显著优于以像素为基础的方法.

blocks.en: These findings establish a new connection between generative architecture and video coding and opens a decoding-free direction for studying and identifying synthetic video through the computational traces of its generation process.
blocks.zh: 这些发现在基因架构和视频编码之间建立了新的联系,并打开了无编码方向,通过生成过程的计算痕迹来研究和识别合成视频.
